feature1.prompt: Update the fast delete query generation logic. When emulating ON DELETE CASCADE via on_delete=models.CASCADE the deletion.Collector performs individual fast delete queries for each related field. The feature requires that, instead of issuing separate DELETE statements for each relationship, queries for the same table are combined into a single DELETE statement using OR conditions. For example, separate queries for different foreign key fields should be merged into a single query such as 'DELETE FROM entry WHERE created_by_id = :id OR updated_by = :id'. This improvement involves enhancing the related_objects method to support multiple related fields and to generate the appropriate query modifiers accordingly.
feature1.hint_texts: Enhance the related_objects method by updating its signature to accept multiple related fields and returning a QuerySet with select_related applied to all the specified field names. Ensure that both the implementation in django/contrib/admin/utils.py and the corresponding usage in django/db/models/deletion.py are aligned with the new API. The focus is on combining fast delete queries by table, so pay special attention to the construction of the OR conditions in the generated query. Coordinate with the developers working on the Collector refactor to ensure consistency in how deletion queries are batched.
feature1.entrypoint: Files to modify: django/contrib/admin/utils.py (update the related_objects method) and django/db/models/deletion.py (update the related_objects method used within the fast delete processing logic). Start by altering the method signature to receive 'related_model' and 'related_fields' and adjust the QuerySet to use select_related with the list of field names.

feature2.prompt: Refactor the internal data handling of deletion.Collector to improve fast delete operations. The Collector class currently uses basic dictionaries to manage model instances, field updates, and deletion dependencies. This feature requires refactoring these data structures to use defaultdict for improved clarity and efficiency. The improved implementation should streamline the batching of delete queries and maintain correct behavior when multiple foreign key relationships are involved.
feature2.hint_texts: Refactor the Collector class in django/db/models/deletion.py by replacing the native dictionaries for data, field_updates, and dependencies with defaultdict (with appropriate default factory functions). Update the get_del_batches method to accept a list of fields and use the new structure for managing batch sizes. Also, review the add and collect methods to ensure that the modifications integrate seamlessly with the fast delete operations. Verify that the overall deletion logic is maintained and that performance is improved with these internal changes.
feature2.entrypoint: File to modify: django/db/models/deletion.py. Begin with the Collector class's __init__ method to initialize data structures (data, field_updates, dependencies) using defaultdict. Next, adjust the get_del_batches method to work with a list of field names and refactor the add, add_field_update, and collect methods accordingly. Use the new imports from collections (defaultdict) and functools (partial) as necessary.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features involve modifications to the deletion logic within django/db/models/deletion.py. In addition, changes to the related_objects method in django/contrib/admin/utils.py are shared, affecting how fast delete queries are generated.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Integrate Feature1 and Feature2 by ensuring that the enhanced query generation in the related_objects method works seamlessly with the refactored Collector internals. Both features must be coordinated so that the batching and combining of fast delete queries are maintained correctly after the refactor. Comprehensive integration testing is required to validate that the combined queries and updates to internal data structures interact as expected.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers implementing Feature1 and Feature2 should discuss the new method signatures and internal data structure changes to ensure consistent API usage. Coordination is needed regarding how the Collector class processes and batches fast delete operations. Regular meetings and code reviews should be set up to address potential integration issues and ensure that changes in one feature do not regress functionality in the other.
